case.title: Dinitration: approved acid-compatible microflow path
case.protocol:
RAW BATCH PROTOCOL:
An aniline derivative was treated with nitric acid in the industrial batch solvent at 60 C for 4 h. Nitric acid served as nitrating reagent and acid catalyst. The dinitrated product was obtained in 89% yield.

OBJECTIVE:
Design a conservative microflow nitration screen with segregated feeds, controlled mixing, and immediate quench.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Use only the listed inventory.
- Use two segregated feeds before the micromixer.
- Use the approved PTFE 5 mL microcoil.
- Operate at 60 C and include immediate quench.

analogies.summary: This record describes a condensation reaction proceeding via nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) mechanism using DIPEA as base in DMA solvent. The reaction was performed in a Vapourtec R4+ flow reactor with a 10 mL reactor volume at 250°C with a 30-minute residence time and 1.0 mL/min flow rate, achieving 69% yield at 0.5 M concentration. The batch baseline was conducted at room temperature (25°C) for 30 minutes and achieved the same 69% yield. Flow chemistry enabled the use of significantly higher reaction temperature (250°C vs 25°C) while maintaining the same residence time and yield, suggesting improved reaction kinetics and process intensification through better heat transfer control in the continuous flow system.

chemistry.scope_summary: The synthesis involves condensation of 2-fluorobenzaldehydes with methylhydrazine to produce substituted indazoles. The reaction conditions were optimized for a range of electron-withdrawing and electron-donating groups. The methodology allows for rapid synthesis and scalability, suitable for generating a range of indazole analogues.

analogies.summary: This process involves an intramolecular nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) cyclization reaction using DBU as base in diglyme solvent. The flow process operates at 220°C with a 30-minute residence time in a tubular plug flow reactor made of Hastelloy tubing (3.175 mm ID, 16.4 mL volume), using an HPLC pump at 8.3 mL/min flow rate and requiring a back-pressure regulator at 51.7 bar. Flow conditions achieved a 6-fold process intensification compared to batch, reducing reaction time from 3 hours to 30 minutes while increasing temperature from 140°C to 220°C. The flow setup enabled access to higher temperatures and pressures that would be challenging in batch mode, though the yield decreased slightly from 67% to 62%.

chemistry.scope_summary: Developed a continuous flow method using DBU in diglyme at high temperature to enable rapid scaleup of an enantiopure benzodioxan intermediate, achieving high product purity while suppressing undesired regioisomer formation.

optimization_table.key_findings: 10 mL/g diglyme, 220 °C, DBU 2.6 eq. gave 63% yield, 99% purity, 95% ee.

full_record.notes: Flow rate and total residence time derived from flow optimized data. BPR presence noted from figure but unavailable in extracted data. Complete extraction confidence is 85%.

analogies.summary: This transition-metal-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction was performed using both homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis in acetonitrile solvent with triethylamine as base. The flow process utilized an X-Cube Flash reactor with stainless steel tubing (1.0 mm ID, 4.0 mL volume) operated at 170°C with a 10-minute residence time and 0.4 mL/min flow rate under 10 bar back pressure. Both batch (150°C, 5 hours, microwave heating) and flow conditions achieved 94% yield at 0.65 M concentration. The flow process provided a significant time advantage, reducing reaction time from 5 hours to 10 minutes (30-fold acceleration) while allowing operation at higher temperature (170°C vs 150°C) and eliminating the need for microwave heating. The back pressure regulator was essential for maintaining single-phase liquid conditions at the elevated temperature.

chemistry.scope_summary: Mizoroki–Heck couplings of aryl iodides and bromides with butyl acrylate were successfully performed in both batch/microwave and continuous-flow modes using a homogeneous Pd(OAc)2 catalyst with high yield and selectivity.

optimization_table.key_findings: The Mizoroki–Heck coupling using 0.01 mol % Pd(OAc)2 at 170°C achieved full conversion and high selectivity.
